This Mfa Is Filed Under Section 173(1) Of Mv Act,
Praying To Allow The Above Misc. First Appeal And
Consequently Modify The Judgment And Award Dated
16.03.2015 Passed By The Learned Senior Civil Judge
And Member Mact-Ix At- Basavana Bagewadi In Mvc
No.144/2012 And Consequently Be Pleased To Enhance
The Compensation Amount From Rs.6,50,818/- To
Rs.19,80,000/- Along With Interest At The Rate Of 12%.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Arguments, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimants are in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT-IX, Basavana Bagewadi (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.144/2012, vide judgment and award dated 16.03.2015.
2.
The claimants are the legal heirs/dependents of deceased Channappa, aged 65 years and an agricultural labourer.
The claimants claimed that on 09.10.2011 when NC: 2023:KHC-K:1347 the deceased was walking, he was hit by a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA.28/S.30001.

As a result, the deceased suffered hemorrhagic contusion on the right tempo frontal region with sub-dural bleeding in the right frontal temporal parietal region, sub-dural bleeding in tentorium and falx linear fracture of both frontal temporal, left parietal and left occipital bone, grievous fractural injuries to left shoulder/hand and grievous injuries on left leg, left knee and left ear and also sustained other injuries all over the body.

The deceased was shifted to the Government hospital,
Ronihal, where he was administered first aid and thereafter, referred to a neurological center at Dr.Prashant Katakol's Health City Hospital, Vijayapur.
The deceased thereafter died due to the injuries suffered in the accident on 21.07.2012.
The claimants therefore filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the death of Channappa from the owner and insurer of the motorcycle.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1347 Smt.Neelakka W/O Channappa Patil And ... vs Shri.Vilas S/O Tatesab Buyite And Anr on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55050183/
2 3. The owner of the motorcycle denied the accident and claimed that there was no negligence on his part in riding the motorcycle.
He also alleged that the motorcycle was not involved in the accident.
He denied the age and income of the deceased.
He contended that the vehicle was covered by a policy of insurance.
4. The insurer denied the averments made in claim petition and claimed that the injuries suffered by the deceased did not lead to his death.
It also alleged that the accident was due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
5. Claimant No.1 was examined as P.W.1 and she also examined the doctor, who treated the deceased as P.W.2 and another witness as P.W.2 and P.W.3 and marked Exs.P.1 to P.15.

The insurer examined one of its officials as D.W.1 and marked its policy of insurance as Ex.R.1.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1347 6.

Based on oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that P.W.3 was an eyewitness, who supported the case of the claimants and he deposed that it was the rider of the motorcycle who was negligent and was responsible for the accident.

It also held that PW.2, the doctor who treated the deceased deposed that the deceased was treated between 09.10.2011 to 18.11.2011 and that at the time of his discharge, the claimant suffered restriction in movement of limb on the left side.
He also deposed that the deceased was on ryles tube feeds and he had to follow up the treatment.
He deposed that the deceased was again admitted on 09.03.2012 and was discharged on 15.03.2012.

The deceased continued to be on tube feeds and on foleys catheter and he suffered hemiplegia on left side and thereafter, he was admitted on 08.06.2012 with post traumatic epileptics with neurogenic pulmonary oedema and was discharged on 15.06.2012.
The deceased was on endotracheal tube with oxygen support.
P.W.2 deposed that though the deceased was conscious at the time of discharge, there was no limb NC: 2023:KHC-K:1347 movement and he continued to be on tube feeds.
The Tribunal therefore, held that the deceased died due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
However, it noticed from the case sheet that the deceased was a chronic alcoholic/smoker and had difficulty in getting up due to weakness in the limbs for almost 15 years prior to the accident.

Therefore, it held that the death was not entirely due to the accident and hence, the claim petition for compensation for the death did not survive as the claimants did not press the claim petition claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by the deceased.
The Tribunal therefore, merely awarded a compensation of Rs.6,50,818/- being the medical expenses incurred by the claimants and directed the insurer to pay the compensation.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants are in appeal.
7. Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the accident in question is not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that the deceased suffered injuries when he NC: 2023:KHC-K:1347 was dashed against by a motorcycle.
Therefore, the finding of the Tribunal that the deceased was not in a position to even walk is without any basis.
He contended that the deceased was hale and healthy in the year 2011 and what is mentioned in the case sheet is not a fact.
He submitted that the deceased was 55 years old and was contributing his income for the wellbeing of the family.

He submits that at Smt.Neelakka W/O Channappa Patil And ... vs Shri.Vilas S/O Tatesab Buyite And Anr on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55050183/
3 the time of accident, the claimant Nos.2 and 3 were students and were dependent on the deceased and hence, the finding of the Tribunal that the deceased was suffering from illness due to his habits is without any basis.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer contended that Ex.P.1 was the discharge summery,
which disclosed that the deceased was a chronic alcoholic and a smoker and had difficulty in getting up.
He therefore, submits that the death of the deceased cannot be attributed to the injuries suffered in the accident.
Hence, he submitted that the death was attributable to the habits of the deceased.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.
10. The claim petition disclosed that the claimant Nos.2 and 3 were students at the time of accident i.e., on 09.10.2011.
It also shows that the deceased was walking back towards Ronihal and that the motorcycle in question dashed against him, resulting in injuries to him.
Therefore, there is no justification to hold that the deceased was not in a position to get up and or that he was not in a position to meet the emotional and financial needs to the family.

From the year 2011 till the year 2012, when he died, he was under constant medical treatment and the evidence of P.W.2 gives an image of the pathetic condition of the deceased and therefore, it can easily be held that he died due to the injuries suffered in the accident.

The fact that he was treated last on 15.06.2012 and that he died on NC: 2023:KHC-K:1347 21.07.2012 makes it more than apparent that the death was due to the injuries suffered by the deceased in the accident.

The Tribunal committed an error in holding that the death was not due to the injuries suffered in the accident, but due to his pre-accident illness,
which was without any basis.
Consequently, the claimants were entitled to be compensated under the loss of dependency on the deceased as well as the loss of consortium and other conventional heads.

In that view of the matter, the compensation to which the claimants are entitled is re- determined by considering the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and factoring 10% loss of future prospects.
Since the deceased was married and he left behind three dependents, 1/3rd of the income deserves to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to the following compensation:
- 10 -  NC: 2023:KHC-K:1347  Sl.No. Heads Amount  1. Loss of dependency Rs.4,75,200/-

4  (Rs.6,000/- + Rs.600  (10%) = Rs.6,600/-
 x 1/3 x 12 x 9)
 2. Medical expenses Rs.6,50,818/-
 3. Loss of spousal Rs.44,000/-
 consortium to  claimant No.1  4. Loss of parental Rs.88,000/-
 consortium to  5. Loss of estate, Rs.33,000/
 funeral expenses and  transportation  expenses
11. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.6,50,818/- to Rs.12,91,018/-.

The enhanced compensation shall be paid by the insurer of the offending vehicle along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1347 the date of realization excluding the period of delay of 529 days in filing this appeal.

The insurer of the offending vehicle shall deposit the enhanced compensation and interest before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of a receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be kept in a fixed deposit in the name of claimant No.1 in any Nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
